# Sirach Chapter 27 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 27 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**27:1** Many have sinned for the sake of a trifling gain, and one who seeks to multiply wealth averts his eye.

**27:2** Like a peg driven between two stones, so sin will wedge itself between buying and selling.

**27:3** Unless a man holds fast in the fear of the LORD, his house will soon be overthrown.

**27:4** In the shaking of a sieve the refuse stays behind; so in a man's reflection his faults remain.

**27:5** The furnace tests the work of the potter; so the test of a man is in his reasoning.

**27:6** The fruit of a tree reveals how it was tended; so the word of a man reveals the thoughts of his heart.

**27:7** Before you hear, do not praise a man; for this is the testing of persons.

**27:8** If you pursue righteousness, you will attain it, and put it on like a robe of glory.

**27:9** Birds of a kind settle among their own kind, and truth returns to those who practice it.

**27:10** A lion lies in wait for its prey; so sin waits for those who practice lawlessness.

**27:11** The discourse of a devout man is always wisdom, but a foolish man changes like the moon.

**27:12** Among men without understanding, limit your time; but among thoughtful men spend it freely.

**27:13** The conversation of fools is offensive, and their laughter wallows in the licentiousness of sin.

**27:14** The swearing of a man given to many oaths makes the hair stand on end, and their quarrels are enough to stop the ears.

**27:15** The bloodshed of those who quarrel with each other is evil, and their abuse becomes intolerable to the ear.

**27:16** Whoever betrays secrets destroys faithfulness, and will find no true friend.

**27:17** Love your friend and keep faith with him; but if you have revealed his secrets, do not go after him.

**27:18** For as one who has killed his enemy, so you have killed the friendship of your neighbor.

**27:19** And as a bird you have released from your hand, so you have let your friend go; you will not catch him again.

**27:20** Do not pursue him, for he has gone far off; he has escaped like a gazelle from a snare. For his soul is wounded — there is no longer any healing, for he has been insulted and reviled.

**27:21** As for silver and gold, a slip may yet restore them; but as for you, you have been found out for the sake of your neighbor's words.

**27:22** A man who winks craftily — who will escape him?

**27:23** Before your face he speaks sweet words and admires your discourse; but afterward he will twist his mouth and speak slander about your words.

**27:24** Many things I have hated, but nothing equal to him; even the LORD will hate him.

**27:25** Whoever throws a stone straight up — it falls on his own head; a treacherous blow wounds the one who strikes it.

**27:26** Whoever digs a pit — into it he will fall; whoever sets a snare — in it he will be caught.

**27:27** Whoever does evil — it will roll back upon him, and he will not know from where it has come upon him.

**27:28** Mockery and reproach are the lot of the arrogant man, and vengeance lies in wait for him like a lion.

**27:29** Those who rejoice in the downfall of the devout will be caught in a trap, and pain will consume them before they die.

**27:30** Wrath and anger — these too are abominations, and a sinful man will cling to them.
